notes.headline: Nothing technically wrong here — this master measures clean at -10.72 LUFS integrated with -2.16 dBTP of true-peak room.
notes.summary: MixCheck found no technical problems in this 0:40 stereo master, so it scores 10.0/10 and reads as release-ready. Loudness sits at -10.72 LUFS integrated with 5.15 LU of range and 8.6 dB peak-to-loudness, so it's loud without being flattened. Stereo behavior is well controlled: L/R correlation 0.78, low-end correlation 0.78, only 0.51 dB lost in mono, and the sides are balanced within -0.04 dB. There's nothing to fix — the next step is trusting your ears on a couple of playback systems rather than reaching for processing.
listen_for: Play it back in mono on a phone or single speaker and confirm nothing thins out — the analysis says you only lose 0.51 dB, so it should hold up.
Check the low end on a system with real bass extension; low-end correlation of 0.78 suggests it should translate, but confirm the bass stays centered and solid.
Listen for level shifts across the 0:40 — 5.15 LU of loudness range means there's real dynamic movement, so make sure it feels intentional.
strengths: True peak at -2.16 dBTP leaves safe margin for lossy encoding on streaming platforms.
8.6 dB peak-to-loudness at -10.72 LUFS means you got level without crushing the transients.
Left/right balance within -0.04 dB and 0.78 correlation — the stereo image is centered and phase-coherent.
